title: Correctness of the input simulation step
statement: Let $C_w,c_w\in\mathbb{N}$, let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, and let $x$ be a finite Boolean input. Suppose an atom assignment is good for every bounded choice of time, work-tape address, and input address in the sense of the stated local checks. If $t+1<2^W$, the assignment correctly represents the computation through time $t$, and $d$ is an integer with $|d|\le |x|+1$, then its represented input-tape symbol at offset $d$ after $t+1$ steps equals the symbol at offset $d$ in the actual computation of $M$ on $x$ after $t+1$ steps.
hypotheses_covered: A finite Turing machine $M$ over the Boolean alphabet
An atom assignment satisfying all bounded local checks
Correct representation of the computation through time $t$
caveat: The exact predicates AllGood and Correct are complex definitions omitted from the supplied informal vocabulary; the statement summarizes their computational meaning, but that summary may not capture every formal detail.
